correctness.rationale: Schatten Hölder gives the universal lower bound. For a normal target T=U|T|, the commuting split X=U|T|^{r/p}, Y=|T|^{r/q} satisfies XY=YX=T and ||X||_p||Y||_q=||T||_r. Tensoring with any S_p,S_q rank-one commutator factorization gives T tensor P with factor-cost multiplied by exactly ||T||_r; finite-rank normal T is unitarily equivalent to T tensor P on an infinite-dimensional Hilbert space. Brown's nonzero-trace obstruction supplies the forbidden half-space.

originality.rationale: Anderson--Brown and Dykema--Figiel--Weiss--Wodzicki already provide the Schatten existence threshold and are treated as prior art. Tran gives operator-norm commutator cost and Liu gives operator-norm compact-factor bounds and tensorization. Searches and inspected relevant sources did not locate the mixed infimum-product Schatten gauge estimate Gamma_{p,q}(T) comparable to ||T||_r with constants independent of rank for normal targets. Older operator-ideal literature remains a residual risk for equivalent terminology.

value.rationale: The result turns a qualitative ideal-membership threshold into a rank-free quantitative factorization estimate on a broad structured class, identifies the natural target norm S_r, and isolates a reusable tensor-transfer mechanism. For nonzero positive finite-rank targets it packages the classical Brown--Anderson boundary as a normed factorization phase transition.
